title: Atomic-Scale Insights into Interfaces in Hafnium Oxide Ferroelectric Thin Films
content: Hafnium oxide (HfO2)–based ferroics have emerged as a promising class of materials for next-generation memory and logic applications due to their robust ferroelectricity, high scalability, simple chemical composition, and high compatibility with semiconductor technology [1]. However, the ferroelectric non-centrosymmetric orthorhombic (O) phase in HfO2 is metastable and requires external factors such as oxygen vacancies and strain for stabilization, making it challenging to fully understand the material’s ferroelectric behavior. Moreover, despite its simple chemical composition, HfO2 exhibits a complex phase diagram, where multiple stable and metastable phases with similar structural features can form. In particular, the frequent coexistence and intricate interplay of these phases introduce additional complexity, further obscuring the fundamental mechanisms governing its ferroelectric properties. In this sense, atomic-scale investigations—particularly at phase interfaces—can provide critical insights into the origin of ferroelectricity in HfO2 and enable the targeted optimization of its properties.
